![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/dab5266e6607ac13c0cd9f7cd2dd58ada9659960beb596c19f7ba3e1c00cf953.png)

Find the area $A$ of the shaded region that lies between the polar curves $r=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $r=\frac{3}{2},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we find the values of $\theta $ for which the two curves intersect:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{3}{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ]:$

$$
\theta =-\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}
$$

To determine which is the inner function and which is the outer, let's draw an arrow from the origin that passes through the shaded region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/0b5499cbbe756a5696e67178dfde8a11ea6a7f462fe2d6c17de6299dc621fdff.png)

The arrow

- *enters* the region through the inner function $r=\frac{3}{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $r=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

To find the area, we use the formula

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where

$$
\,{\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3},\,\text{ and }\,{\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}((3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}-{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}(9{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -\frac{9}{4})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}(\frac{9}{2}+\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\frac{9}{4})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}(\frac{9}{4}+\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9}{4}\theta +\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )){|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((\frac{9}{4}\cdot \frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}))-(\frac{9}{4}\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{2\pi }{3}))) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}+\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
